summary.oneLiner: Westlife Foodworld is the McDonald's master franchisee for West and South India, operating 478 restaurants across 78 cities through its wholly owned subsidiary Hardcastle Restaurants Private Limited.
summary.business: Westlife Foodworld is a holding company that, through its wholly owned subsidiary Hardcastle Restaurants Private Limited (HRPL) — the Development Licensee / Master Franchisee of McDonald's — owns and operates McDonald's quick service restaurants across West and South India. currentContext.expansion: Westlife expanded its network at what management calls a record pace in FY 2025-26: store presence rose to 478 restaurants from 438, with 48 restaurants added during the year, and city presence rose to 78 from 69 — an entry into 9 new cities. Expansion is deliberately 'prudent expansion beyond metro cities, alongside continued densification in key markets', supported by robust site-selection capability and a cluster-led strategy across high-potential micro-markets including drive-thrus and high-street formats. The format mix is diversified across dine-in, drive-thrus (25% drive-thru mix), McCafes and Experience-of-the-Future (EOTF) stores, with 100% penetration of McCafe and EOTF formats on the eligible base, plus dessert kiosks, McBreakfast and select 24x7 restaurants. The stated roadmap is to scale the network from 478 to 580-630 restaurants by 2027, through a balanced mix of new market entry and cluster densification, and management says the Company 'remains on track' to that number. Alongside store additions, the Company reports continued investment in technology, McCafe, modern store formats and delivery capabilities, in self-ordering kiosks (SOKs) and in the McDonald's / McDelivery apps, and in a fully integrated temperature-controlled farm-to-fork supply chain. On sustainability-linked capex, BRSR Principle 2 states the Company 'continues to undertake sustainability-linked capex as part of its broader restaurant and operational investments, including initiatives related to solar power, energy efficiency and water conservation', but that 'since these costs are embedded within overall capex, they are not separately identifiable or allocated' — an explicit refusal to quantify, not an omission. The same disclosure states the Company does not incur any significant R&D expense, relying instead on strategic partnerships with value-chain partners (including a collaboration with CSIR-CFTRI on nutrient-rich offerings such as millet-based buns and a plant-based Protein Slice). Manufacturing footprint is a stated NIL: BRSR Section A item 18 prints 0 plants nationally and 0 internationally, against 1 head office and 478 restaurants (479 locations), and 11 states served with 0 international countries — the asset base is restaurants, not plants.

risks.note: Ranked the top material issue. Any lapse in food safety protocols could lead to legal liabilities, damage to brand reputation and loss of customer trust; proper handling and hygiene are critical to prevent contamination and foodborne illness. Mitigation: food safety protocols embedded across menu development, packaging, distribution and restaurant operations; monthly sensory evaluation of key products and quarterly for non-key products; technology and automation aligned to food-safety standards. Stated financial implication: negative.

risks.risk: Responsible sourcing and supplier practices (supply-chain concentration and disruption)
risks.note: Westlife sources ingredients from many suppliers, so food safety depends on supply-chain management, and the business affects environmental health, animal welfare and livelihoods. Disruptions or inconsistencies in supplier practices directly hit menu quality and availability. Stated financial implication: negative — timely availability of products can be compromised by value-chain disruption, and operational inconsistency damages reputation and profitability. Mitigation: sustainable/ethical sourcing, supplier selection on quality, sustainable farming and labour rights, and Supply Chain Human Rights Audits (SCHRA) for every supplier covering business integrity, child labour and forced labour.

risks.risk: Nutrition and responsible marketing / regulatory scrutiny of food labelling
risks.note: Evolving consumer awareness demands accessible nutritional information and clear labelling; failure damages brand reputation and attracts regulatory scrutiny, impacting sales and profitability. Mitigation: artificial colours, preservatives and flavourings eliminated from select/most items; allergen and nutritional information displayed in-store and on the McDelivery app; fat and sodium reduced in key products; strict advertising guidelines; nutrition-focused innovation including the Multi-Millets Bun and Protein Plus Slice.

A large volume of customer data is captured for operational purposes through the McDonald's app, McDelivery and self-ordering kiosks — a risk that scales with the Company's own digital strategy, given digital channels contribute 76% of sales. A breach can lead to fines, penalties and reputational damage. Mitigation: Cybersecurity and Privacy Policy on the intranet, robust security measures, and cyber security explicitly within the Risk Management Committee's monitoring mandate.

The Company itself states the business is 'relatively energy-intensive due to usage of commercial kitchen appliances and high volumes', with temperature-controlled dining areas. Stated financial implication: negative — physical assets such as facilities and logistics infrastructure are at risk of damage from extreme weather events with substantial repair and replacement cost, and regulatory change could raise operating and compliance costs. Mitigation: energy-efficiency upgrades, process optimisation to reduce carbon footprint, and renewable energy including solar. Note the tension with the standalone Directors' Report line that 'the operations of your Company are not energy intensive' and that capital investment on energy-conservation equipment was NIL — that statement is made for the listed holding entity, with the measures attributed to the subsidiary HRPL.

risks.risk: Human rights across own operations and the value chain
risks.note: Human-rights violations can cause operational delays, lawsuits, poor employee satisfaction and reputational damage. Mitigation: policies, training and regular audits; zero-tolerance approach to compulsory and forced labour including human trafficking and child labour; human-rights clauses in all business agreements and contracts.

risks.risk: Ethics and compliance in an evolving food-regulation regime
risks.note: Compliance with evolving food and nutrition regulations, legal norms and ethical standards has a direct impact on business operations and brand image. Mitigation: Standards of Business Conduct, Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption Policy, Code of Conduct and whistleblower mechanisms, an internal committee reviewing food-nutrition compliance, and 100% of operations assessed for corruption-related risks within the ERM framework. Nil disciplinary actions for bribery/corruption against directors, KMPs or employees, and nil conflict-of-interest complaints, in FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25.

risks.risk: Water and waste management (resource and regulatory exposure at restaurant level)
risks.note: Water conservation is stated as necessary for regulatory compliance, lower operating cost and business continuity, with water shortages capable of interrupting operations and breaching regulatory norms; waste from daily operations is called a significant environmental challenge in the industry, exposing the Company to fines, higher disposal costs and increased expenses. Mitigation: waterless urinals, reuse of RO-rejected water, high-water-recovery RO systems in all restaurants, spray faucets (stated to reduce water consumption by 50-80%), packaging optimisation, safe disposal and operations training.

Not labelled a risk but stated as the operating reality: the Company entered FY 2025-26 'amid a subdued consumption environment, with discretionary spending and eating-out frequency remaining under pressure', and describes a 'challenging operating environment' and 'value-sensitive' market throughout. Guest counts only returned to positive comparable growth in the latter part of the year. Industry outlook adds that operators must navigate 'ongoing cost pressures' and that nearly 75% of QSR customers now prioritise value-led offerings, structurally capping pricing power.

STRUCTURAL CONCENTRATION, not labelled as a risk by the Company. BRSR Section A discloses that 100% of turnover comes from one activity (Quick Service Restaurants) and one product line (Sale of Food and Beverages), delivered entirely through one wholly owned subsidiary (HRPL) under a single licensed brand (McDonald's), in 11 states of West and South India, with 0 international locations and exports not applicable. The listed entity itself is a Core Investment Company with three permanent employees on its rolls, so all cash generation depends on HRPL. [Provenance: BRSR Section A items 16-19 and 23 are routed to the profile, governance_entities, registry and capex_expansion bundles, not into this risks_esg bundle.]

STRUCTURAL, not labelled as a risk. BRSR item 22 discloses a permanent-employee turnover rate of 67% total in FY 2025-26 (male 70%, female 61%), against 64% in FY 2024-25 and 67% in FY 2023-24. The Company's own note attributes the level to part-time employees such as college students, and states it is 'relatively higher compared to other industries'. Westlife employs no permanent or contractual workers — all in-store personnel are counted as employees — and had 2,487 apprentices under the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme as on 31 March 2026. [Provenance: BRSR item 22 is routed to the profile, governance_entities and registry bundles, not into this risks_esg bundle.]

risks.risk: Customer-complaint volume as a quality/consistency signal
risks.note: 5,41,425 customer complaints were filed in FY 2025-26 (5,76,918 in FY 2024-25), with nil pending at year-end; the Company states most pertained to missing items, freshness/quality issues and service-related concerns, and that all reported complaints were addressed and resolved. Employee complaints rose to 21 from 3. Investor, shareholder, value-chain-partner and community complaints were nil in both years.

one-line thesis: Westlife delivered steady Q4FY26 growth driven by mid-single-digit guest count recovery and disciplined margin control, with a strategic pivot to everyday value and McCafé habit formation reversing prior stagnation; the acceleration to 60+ annual store openings signals confidence in scalable demand and digital-led volume growth as the new core engine.
financial scorecard: revenue: +9% YoY (INR 6.6B Q4; INR 26.3B FY26); EBITDA/margin: stable at 13.2% (FY26), restaurant op margin +100bps to 20.3%; PAT (rptd): INR 487M Q4 (7.4% margin); PAT (normalized): same as reported (no major one-offs); order book: N/A (no franchise/contractual backlog); net debt: not disclosed (but capex guidance implies controlled leverage)
guidance: revenue growth: target mid-single-digit SSSG; margin: gross margin guidance of 67%+; order inflow: 60+ new restaurants annually; capex/commissioning: 60+ stores to be opened with digital modern design and McCafé integration

hero.industry: QSR / Fast-Food & Coffee Chain Expansion & Digital Habit Formation

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Westlife Foodworld is the McDonald's master franchisee for West and South India, operating 478 restaurants across 78 cities through its wholly owned subsidiary Hardcastle Restaurants Private Limited.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Westlife Foodworld is a holding company that, through its wholly owned subsidiary Hardcastle Restaurants Private Limited (HRPL) — the Development Licensee / Master Franchisee of McDonald's — owns and operates McDonald's quick service restaurants across West and South India. Its network of 478 restaurants in 78 cities is complemented by McDelivery, McCafe, drive-thrus, dessert kiosks, McBreakfast and select 24x7 restaurants, serving a wide consumer base of individuals and families across age groups, income segments and dining occasions (dine-in, takeaway, delivery, drive-thru). The Company itself was classified as a Core Investment Company exempted from registration with the Reserve Bank of India, and promotes the QSR operations through its subsidiary.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Hardcastle Restaurants Private Limited (HRPL) — subsidiary: Wholly owned operating subsidiary; Development Licensee / Master Franchisee of McDonald's, establishing and operating McDonald's restaurants across West and South India; accounts for 100% of turnover. Held since 13 November 2011. Shareholding stated as 100% in BRSR Section A item 23 but as 99.99% in Form AOC-1 Part A ('Extent of shareholding (in percentage)') — the two disclosures differ and both are reproduced rather than reconciled. Participates in the listed entity's Business Responsibility initiatives; a separate Secretarial Audit Report for HRPL is annexed and carries no qualification.
- Westlife ESOS Trust (the 'Trust') — subsidiary: Controlled Trust, 100%, held since 3 March 2022. Established to facilitate the share-based payment scheme covering eligible employees of the Company and its subsidiary; administered alongside the Westlife Development Limited Employee Stock Option (Trust) Scheme 2021 by the Nomination and Remuneration Committee. Classified as 'Controlled Trust' in BRSR and consolidated under Form AOC-1 Part A - Subsidiaries.
- Associates and Joint Ventures — associate: STATED ABSENCE — Form AOC-1 Part B states 'The Group does not have any investment in associates or joint ventures.' The Directors' Report separately states that during the year under review no company has become or ceased to be the Company's subsidiary, joint venture or associate company.
- Ronald McDonald House Charities Foundation India (RMHC India) — related party: Enterprise over which KMP or their relatives are able to exercise significant influence. A Section 8 non-profit, part of a global network, through which the group provides free accommodation and supportive care to families of children undergoing medical treatment.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India GDP growth expected to moderate to ~6.9% in FY 2026-27 from 7.7% in FY 2025-26, on rising input costs, supply-chain disruptions, elevated energy prices and softer global demand; services activity and domestic consumption remain the key growth drivers
- Inflation projected to average ~4.6% in FY 2026-27 with upside risks from energy prices and weather; RBI expected to retain policy flexibility
- Global QSR market estimated at $1.04 trillion in 2025, projected to grow from $1.14 trillion in 2026 to ~$2.50 trillion by 2035, a 9.16% CAGR
- India QSR market expanding from $27.8 billion in 2025 to $30.4 billion in 2026 and $47.3 billion by 2031, a 9.3% CAGR
- Organised food service expected to grow at nearly twice the pace of the unorganised segment and to surpass it by 2030, driven by evolving consumer preferences, formalisation and stronger brand trust (organised CAGR 12-14% vs unorganised 5-7% for 2025-2030)
- Value-driven consumption is the defining trend — nearly 75% of QSR customers prioritise value-led offerings, pushing brands toward combo meals, promotions, loyalty rewards and personalised digital offers
- Convenience-led service models, loyalty and personalisation, nutrition-conscious menu choices, and sustainability/ESG focus named as the four other trends shaping the QSR market
- Key growth drivers cited: favourable demographics (median age under 30), rapid urbanisation and high-footfall infrastructure, rising per-capita disposable income supporting premiumisation and tier 2/tier 3 expansion, technology adoption (app ordering, digital payments, AI-led analytics), menu innovation and localisation, and omnichannel strategy
- These dynamics are stated to support same-store sales growth, enable rapid network expansion and unlock tier 2 / tier 3 opportunity, 'even as operators navigate ongoing cost pressures'
- Company demand narrative for FY 2025-26: entered the year amid a subdued consumption environment with discretionary spending and eating-out frequency under pressure; guest counts stabilised through everyday value, product innovation, digital engagement and hyperlocal marketing; the second half was a clear turning point with positive comparable guest growth late in the year [provenance: the 'Business progress' passage is cut off mid-sentence at 'At the same t' in this bundle — the remainder and the 'Outlook' paragraph were read from the identical MD&A text routed to the profile / capex_expansion / risks_esg bundles]
- FY 2026-27 outlook: management is encouraged by the improving demand environment and the positive guest-count momentum at the close of FY 2025-26, while remaining mindful of the evolving macroeconomic landscape; confident of sustainable, profitable growth over the long term supported by a strong omnichannel platform, robust unit economics and disciplined execution [provenance: back-filled from the sibling bundles as above]
- QSR industry outlook: transition to a disciplined, consumer-centric growth model where success is defined by consistent quality, value perception and seamless experience rather than speed and scale alone; sharper unit economics, operational efficiency and menu simplification expected, with technology and cultural relevance as differentiators

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Westlife expanded its network at what management calls a record pace in FY 2025-26: store presence rose to 478 restaurants from 438, with 48 restaurants added during the year, and city presence rose to 78 from 69 — an entry into 9 new cities. Expansion is deliberately 'prudent expansion beyond metro cities, alongside continued densification in key markets', supported by robust site-selection capability and a cluster-led strategy across high-potential micro-markets including drive-thrus and high-street formats. The format mix is diversified across dine-in, drive-thrus (25% drive-thru mix), McCafes and Experience-of-the-Future (EOTF) stores, with 100% penetration of McCafe and EOTF formats on the eligible base, plus dessert kiosks, McBreakfast and select 24x7 restaurants. The stated roadmap is to scale the network from 478 to 580-630 restaurants by 2027, through a balanced mix of new market entry and cluster densification, and management says the Company 'remains on track' to that number. Alongside store additions, the Company reports continued investment in technology, McCafe, modern store formats and delivery capabilities, in self-ordering kiosks (SOKs) and in the McDonald's / McDelivery apps, and in a fully integrated temperature-controlled farm-to-fork supply chain. On sustainability-linked capex, BRSR Principle 2 states the Company 'continues to undertake sustainability-linked capex as part of its broader restaurant and operational investments, including initiatives related to solar power, energy efficiency and water conservation', but that 'since these costs are embedded within overall capex, they are not separately identifiable or allocated' — an explicit refusal to quantify, not an omission. The same disclosure states the Company does not incur any significant R&D expense, relying instead on strategic partnerships with value-chain partners (including a collaboration with CSIR-CFTRI on nutrient-rich offerings such as millet-based buns and a plant-based Protein Slice). Manufacturing footprint is a stated NIL: BRSR Section A item 18 prints 0 plants nationally and 0 internationally, against 1 head office and 478 restaurants (479 locations), and 11 states served with 0 international countries — the asset base is restaurants, not plants.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Powerful global brand backing — anchored by the McDonald's brand, giving consumer trust, global operating benchmarks and a time-tested model enabling consistency, efficiency and scale
- Distinctive and scalable operating model — multi-category, multi-channel, multi-daypart approach addressing diverse consumption occasions, driving higher throughput and improved asset productivity
- Integrated farm-to-fork, temperature-controlled supply chain ensuring consistent quality, cost efficiency and scalability from sourcing to last-mile delivery; +99% of inputs locally sourced
- Strategic real estate and cluster expansion — robust site-selection capability and cluster-led expansion across high-potential micro-markets including drive-thrus and high-street formats, supporting store economics
- Strong digital and omnichannel ecosystem — McDonald's and McDelivery apps drive 76% of sales digitally, with ~52 million cumulative app downloads and ~3.5 million monthly active users enabling personalised marketing, loyalty and demand forecasting
- Everyday-value platform — Everyday Value Meals at Rs 99 drove strong dine-in traction and reinforced affordability credentials in a value-sensitive market
- Format penetration already built out — 100% EOTF and McCafe penetration on the eligible base, 25% drive-thru mix
- Volume-led, profitable growth engine — affordability drives guest traffic while operating leverage and cost discipline support margin expansion (management characterisation)

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Accounting - gross margin] Processing charges were regrouped from other operating expenses into cost of goods sold; implication is COGS increases, other operating expenses decrease, gross profit and margin decrease, while sales, ROM, EBITDA and PAT are unchanged. On the adjusted basis Q1FY26 gross margin is 67.6% versus 71.6% as originally reported, so reported gross-margin history is not comparable without this adjustment.
- [Accounting - Ind AS 116] The deck presents a full adjusted-versus-reported reconciliation: Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA margin is 7.5% adjusted versus 12.9% reported, and restaurant operating margin 13.3% adjusted versus 18.6% reported, the gap being lease accounting under Ind AS 116.
- [Exceptional items] Exceptional items are defined as one-time gain/expense on account of assets written off pertaining to restaurant relocation/closure.
- [Corporate] Operations are run through Hardcastle Restaurants Pvt. Ltd.; the company is listed as NSE: WESTLIFE and BSE: 505533.
